selected_primary_idea.title: Physical Compute-Envelope Contract (PEC)
selected_primary_idea.summary: A resource-accounting protocol that evaluates useful computational-throughput claims under a named workload, accuracy, reliability, architecture, energy, thermal, spatial, communication, memory, and I/O boundary.
selected_primary_idea.scientific_object: workload x correctness target x reliability target x architecture x physical resource cards
selected_primary_idea.central_hypothesis: A layered, contract-bounded envelope distinguishes supported from unsupported processing-speed claims more reliably than a component-rate or benchmark-only metric.
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: Each claimed useful rate is constrained by explicit transition, signal, thermal, memory, reliability, and I/O cards, with inapplicable terms marked rather than silently assumed.
falsifiers: contract cannot separate supported from unsupported claims
mandatory cards add no decision value
validated logical throughput violates the disclosed envelope without a changed contract
sampling advantage cannot be represented without universalizing it

competitive_ideas.title: Fault-Tolerance-normalized gate score
competitive_ideas.reason: Useful as a reliability submetric but incomplete without physical transport, thermal, and workload bounds.

high_risk_ideas.title: Attempt a universal closed-form upper bound
high_risk_ideas.reason: Conceptually attractive but likely invalid across computational models and resource assumptions.

rejected_ideas.reason: Frequency is not useful end-to-end throughput.
Violates evidence that quantum processing remains physically constrained and workload-dependent.

mcts_evolution.change: add signal, thermal, memory, I/O cards
separate algorithmic advantage from logical throughput
